title: On the $\mathrm{In_{x}Ga_{1-x}As}$ channel noise in InP HEMTs from 4 K to 300 K
authors: Junjie Li, Justin H. Chen, Austin J. Minnich, Jan Grahn
abstract: The InP high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) is indispensable for low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) in radio astronomy and quantum computing. The composition of the $\mathrm{In_{x}Ga_{1-x}As}$ channel in InP HEMT is known to influence the LNA noise performance. However, the various physical mechanisms responsible for noise generation are not fully characterized and understood. Here, we investigate the $\mathrm{In_{x}Ga_{1-x}As}$ channel noise from 4 K to 300 K for 100-nm gate-length InP HEMTs with channel indium content of 53\%, 60\% and 70\%. Channel noise was quantified by extracting the equivalent drain noise temperature $\mathit{T}_{d}$ using both on-wafer and LNA-based measurements, covering 40-300 K and 4-40 K, respectively. The 60\% indium channel InP HEMT exhibited the lowest channel noise across the full temperature range. The $\mathit{T}_{d}$ extracted from on-wafer characterization was found to obey a parabolic temperature dependence which predicted the $\mathit{T}_{d}$ at 4 K for all InP HEMTs in good agreement with LNA-based measurements. By expressing the channel noise as the sum of one thermal and one excess noise term, it was found that the former increased linearly with ambient temperature and dominated at 300 K. The channel noise at 4 K was determined by the excess noise term and exhibited a non-monotonic dependence on the channel indium content in the InP HEMT. The results suggest that the excess noise in the InP HEMT originates not only from temperature-independent shot noise but also from impact ionization and real-space transfer noise.
summary: This work investigates the temperature dependence of channel noise in InP HEMTs with $\mathrm{In_{x}Ga_{1-x}As}$ channels. By measuring noise from 4 K to 300 K, the authors decompose the total noise into thermal and excess components. They conclude that the excess noise is dominated by impact ionization and real-space transfer effects, not just shot noise, guiding material optimization for low-noise applications.
main_problem: The study aims to fully characterize the physical mechanisms responsible for noise generation in $\mathrm{In_{x}Ga_{1-x}As}$ channels within InP HEMTs across a wide temperature range (4 K to 300 K).
main_result: The excess channel noise at cryogenic temperatures is found to originate not only from shot noise but also significantly from impact ionization and real-space transfer (RST) noise, with the 60% indium composition yielding the lowest overall noise.
method: Noise was quantified by extracting the equivalent drain noise temperature ($T_d$) using both on-wafer characterization at higher temperatures and LNA-based measurements at lower temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is a 100-nm gate-length InP HEMT utilizing an $\mathrm{In_{x}Ga_{1-x}As}$ channel. The noise analysis decomposes the total current noise into temperature-dependent thermal and excess components.
key_observables: Equivalent drain noise temperature ($T_d$), channel current noise power spectral density ($\mathrm{S_{id}}$), and the ratio of thermal to excess noise contributions.
important_parameters: Temperature range (4 K to 300 K); Indium content in the channel ($x=53\%, 60\%, 70\%$); Bias conditions ($V_{ds} = 0.5$ V, $I_d = 5$ mA).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that differences in channel thickness are negligible due to the 2DEG location near the interface.
figures_summary: Figures compare $T_d$ vs. temperature for different indium contents (on-wafer vs. LNA), and show $\mathrm{S_{id}}$ at 4 K versus indium content, illustrating the noise dependence on composition.
paper_structure: The paper systematically measures channel noise across varying temperatures using two complementary setups (on-wafer and LNA). It models the total noise as a sum of thermal and excess terms, analyzes the temperature dependence, and finally attributes the excess noise to specific hot-electron mechanisms based on composition variation.
why_interesting: While focused on semiconductor device physics rather than fundamental quantum dynamics, understanding noise sources in high-frequency transistors is crucial for developing low-noise components required in quantum measurement and sensing applications.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Schematic of the cryogenic noise measurement setup using an LNA module equipped with the InP HEMTs. The LNA is cooled to a temperature between 4 and 40 K inside a cryostat.

Fig. 2. Schematic of the on-wafer noise measurement setup in a cryogenic probe station. The InP HEMT is probed on-wafer at temperatures from 40 to 300 K. The room-temperature measurement chain consists of (1) HMC-T2100 local oscillator, (2) M1-0220-P mixer, (3)–(4) low-noise amplification and attenuation, (5)–(8) bandpass filters, (9) variable attenuator, and (10) U8481A power sensor.

Fig. 3. Equivalent drain noise temperature Td versus ambient temperature for InP HEMTs with channel indium content of 53%, 60%, and 70%, biased at Vds = 0.5 V and Id = 5 mA. Circles and crosses represent Td values extracted from on-wafer and LNA noise measurements, respectively. Dashed lines are parabolic fits to the on-wafer data above 40 K, extrapolated to 4 K. The absence of on-wafer data below 80 K for the 70% indium channel InP HEMT was due to oscillations occurring during probing.
Fig. 5. Thermal noise current PSD Sid,th = 4kBTagds0 versus ambient temperature for InP HEMTs with channel indium content of 53%, 60%, and 70%.

Fig. 4. Channel current noise spectral density Sid at 4 K as a function of indium content x in InxGa1−xAs channel InP HEMTs. Green points show values extracted from LNA noise measurements. Blue points show values extrapolated to 4 K from the Td model fitted to on-wafer measurements (Fig. 3); Error bars represent the combined measurement uncertainties and fitting errors.
